chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that both were asked about what is regarding the slaves.

So they both said: 'There is nothing upon the head [of the slave] anything more than a Sa'a of dates, when the year passes by upon him; and there is nothing upon his price until the year passes by over it'.

key_terms.الرَّأْس: The head [referring to the slave as a unit of assessment]
key_terms.حَالَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: The year passed by upon it [indicating the completion of the lunar year for Zakat]
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement, approximately 3 kg

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for Zakat to become obligatory on a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the nisab (minimum threshold) for Zakat on slaves (Raqiq), establishing that the obligation arises only when the slave possesses wealth equivalent to at least one Sa' of dates held for a full lunar year (Hawl). It distinguishes between the value of the slave's body and their accumulated assets, reflecting the juristic view that Zakat is levied on the slave's personal property rather than the master's ownership. This ruling highlights the economic agency granted to slaves in early Islamic society, allowing them to accumulate and purify wealth independently.
